videos.title: How Are Matches Made? (The Lighter Came First) 🔥
videos.description:
The lighter (1823) was invented three years before the friction match (1826). Logs peeled into millions of sticks, a chemical bath so they don't keep glowing, a wax dip, a head of oxygen salt, sulfur and ground glass. The toxic white phosphorus was banned, and safety matches hide the phosphorus on the box.
Matches or lighter: which do you use? 👇

videos.title: How Is Ice Cream Made? (It Can Be Half Air) 🍦
videos.description:
Milk, cream and sugar heated to kill germs, then a freezer with spinning blades chills it and whips in air. Cheap tubs can be 50% air. A tunnel at -35 °C freezes it fast so the ice crystals stay tiny: that's what makes it smooth, not icy.
What's the best ice cream flavor? 👇

videos.title: How Are Jeans Made? (That Tiny Pocket Was for a Watch) 👖
videos.description:
The tiny pocket was made for pocket watches. Copper rivets were patented in 1873 so work pants wouldn't rip. Blue threads one way and white the other make the inside lighter, the dye only coats the outside so jeans fade, and the faded look comes from tumbling with volcanic stones.
What do you keep in that tiny pocket? 👇
